title: Counter-Selector Wave 29: public resumability and authority-key audit
purpose: Attack the custody and handoff frontier using public release, verification, governance, source, assurance, and continuation records without contacting living subjects or treating reproducibility as authority transfer.

public_reproduction_requires: bounded statement of what reproduction proves
independent_resumability_requires: an operator other than the focal person can acquire the current state
the operator can reproduce or release the object without hidden person-only state
authority, credentials, rollback state, and open decisions are recoverable
the continuation is observed rather than merely planned
direct_handoff_requires: inventory of open decisions and credentials or authority

lanes.public_label: network-transfer project release verification and authority custody

source_records.title: Verify
source_records.artifact_scope: States that release tarballs are signed by Daniel Stenberg while release contents are reproducible and independently verifiable.

source_records.title: curl release candidates
source_records.artifact_scope: Publishes release candidates, cycle timing, and a RELEASE-TOOLS document intended to reproduce release archives.

source_records.title: curl project governance
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines maintainers, security and core teams, lead authority, backup administrators, and a future post-leadership decision surface.

source_records.title: curl releases
source_records.artifact_scope: Shows current canonical release tags and signatures attributed to Daniel Stenberg.

findings: Release contents are reproducible and independently verifiable.
The canonical release signature remains tied to the focal maintainer's key.
Public release tooling does not establish that another operator can publish, rotate authority, or continue from a complete state package.
Backup administrators and a future governance plan remain plans and role surfaces, not observed succession.
counterevidence: Multiple maintainers and teams reduce sole-authorship claims.
Reproduction without release authority, credentials, and open-decision custody is not independent resumability.
next_receipts: canonical release signed and published by a non-focal successor under documented authority

lanes.public_label: embedded-database public source and private assurance boundary

source_records.title: How SQLite Is Tested
source_records.artifact_scope: Describes release checklists, retained checklist history, manual developer verification, fuzzing, regression, and testing tradeoffs.

source_records.title: Quality Management
source_records.artifact_scope: Identifies proprietary TH3 and dbsqlfuzz assets, canonical and backup locations, and private backup surfaces.

source_records.title: SQLite Source Repository
source_records.artifact_scope: Publishes the canonical Fossil source repository and warns that Git repositories are mirrors rather than the urtext.

source_records.title: Release Checklist Application
source_records.artifact_scope: Publishes the checklist application's source and local-running instructions while production checklist state remains separately controlled.

findings: The canonical source, extensive public tests, and checklist tooling are inspectable.
Critical assurance assets, operational checklist updates, and backup state are partly private or developer-restricted.
A third party can inspect and build source, but the public record does not show reproduction of the complete canonical release-assurance state.
No observed project succession or independent successor release is in custody.
counterevidence: Multiple developers can update release checklists.
Retained checklist history creates strong auditability.
Public source and auditability do not expose every assurance asset, authority key, or canonical release decision.
next_receipts: independent reproduction of a canonical release using the full required assurance state
observed maintainer succession with preserved release authority
public inventory of hidden release dependencies and rollback state

source_records.title: FAQ: General
source_records.artifact_scope: Attributes original framework extraction to Adrian Holovaty and Simon Willison, records the open-source release, and states that an international volunteer team now runs the project.

source_records.title: Django Core Developers
source_records.artifact_scope: Lists Simon Willison in the former Django core team while preserving a larger historical contributor structure.

source_records.title: Django teams
source_records.artifact_scope: Lists current teams, paid fellows, mergers, releasers, and other distributed project responsibilities.

source_records.title: Django release process
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines time-based release cycles, release management, branches, tags, and release authority independent of the original co-creator.

source_records.title: django/django
source_records.artifact_scope: Shows an active current repository with extensive history and current contributors long after the focal co-creator's former-core status.

findings: A framework co-created by the focal person was open-sourced and now continues under an international volunteer, fellow, merger, releaser, and governance structure.
The focal person is preserved as a former core contributor while the repository and release process continue without relying on his current authority.
This is founder-independent collective continuation at project scope.
The public record does not isolate a Simon-authored outgoing state package, recipient acknowledgment, or direct handoff event.
counterevidence: The original object was co-created and employer-supported.
Open-source release and later community continuation involve many actors and do not establish sole-person custody.
Current project independence does not prove that the focal person personally designed or executed the transition.
next_receipts: attributable outgoing project-state package from the focal co-creator
evidence linking the focal person to deliberate independent resumability

lanes.public_label: sensitive-data service open-code and team-transition resumability

source_records.title: Have I Been Pwned 2.0 is Now Live
source_records.artifact_scope: Describes the public UX repository, multiple named collaborators, repeated releases, Azure and Cloudflare dependencies, and the still-founder-led service launch.

source_records.title: ux-rebuild initial commit
source_records.artifact_scope: Creates a public repository explicitly intended for collaboration on the UX rebuild.

source_records.title: API documentation discussion
source_records.artifact_scope: Shows public design input and maintainer participation around API documentation choices.

source_records.title: HIBP Terms of Use
source_records.artifact_scope: Identifies the operating company and service authority while preserving the founder and CEO role.

findings: Public code, discussions, named collaborators, and repeated releases expose meaningful team transition and review surfaces.
The public repository covers a collaboration and UX surface, not the complete sensitive-data service, credentials, queues, databases, partner intake, or incident state.
The service remains operated by a company with the focal person identified as founder and CEO.
No observed independent service continuation, successor release authority, or resumable state package is public.
counterevidence: Named collaborators and public discussions defeat a sole-author narrative.
Open code and multiple releases improve inspectability.
Cloud, company, partner, data, and founder dependencies remain material and untransferred.
next_receipts: independent operator runbook covering data, credentials, queues, incident state, and rollback
observed service operation during focal-person absence

disagreements.expansive_position: Anyone can reproduce and verify the release, so custody and handoff may be supported.
disagreements.adversarial_position: Canonical publishing authority and signature remain person-keyed; reproduction does not transfer authority, credentials, or open decisions.

disagreements.expansive_position: Public source, checklists, and testing documentation make the project independently resumable.
disagreements.adversarial_position: Critical assurance assets, canonical controls, and operational checklist state remain restricted or privately backed up.

disagreements.expansive_position: The project continues without the focal co-creator, so person-level custody should be added.
disagreements.adversarial_position: Continuation is collective and source-addressable, but the focal person's outgoing package, recipient, and transition action are not isolated.

disagreements.expansive_position: Public code and named collaborators establish handoff and reduced founder dependency.
disagreements.adversarial_position: The public surface omits full service data, credentials, incident state, partner intake, and authority transfer.

next_action: Prepare artifact-only resumability exports and continue public acquisition for observed successor releases, authority rotation, recipient-acknowledged state packages, and externally reproducible operations without contacting source subjects.
